scene noun

a sight, what is happening before one’s eyes

also sight, spectacle, a sad scene, a happy scene

classical

Cic. Phil. 10.8
Verg. A. 6.37

spectāculum, spectāculī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a sight, a spectacle

Anything that is there to be seen, a sad sight as much as a fine one; also a public show, games or a play (see performance).

Other words

  • faciēs, faciēī f. — the look, the appearance of a thing

    noun, fifth declension · also used · classical · Sall. C. 31.1: immūtāta faciēs urbis erat (Lewis & Short); Tac. A. 4.67: loci (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The look of a place, how things stand there: in Sallust, the whole scene in the city had changed. First of all a face, then the form and look of anything (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Ō spectāculum illud nōn modo hominibus sed undīs ipsīs et lītoribus lūctuōsum!

    Oh, that scene, a grief not only to men but to the very waves and shores!Cic. Phil. 10.8

  • nōn hoc ista sibi tempus spectācula poscit

    this is no time for looking at the sightsVerg. A. 6.37

See also scene, position, performance, view.
